ac:layout-cell.h1: Shared Platform Connectivity and Routing Solution Specification
ac:layout-cell.p: Terminology follows the shared e-invoicing glossary. This is a proposed logical design. It establishes a reviewable shared foundation, not a deployed service, an approved external interface or permission for Sage to launch as an operator.

Implement one shared connection and routing foundation for two uses in Spain: Sage software connects a business to its external private provider; later, the Sage private-platform proposition exchanges with public and other private platforms. Products and partners use the common access contract; selected adapters execute the supported external interfaces. Adding an operator role must not create a second connection registry, route engine or invoice history.

“Build once” describes reuse of shared behaviour. It does not mean one credential, endpoint, connection record or deployment can serve every role. A provider's customer interface and platform-interconnection interface may have different permissions, trust, registration and transport requirements. Qualify each separately and reuse an adapter only where its actual contract fits.

tr.td: PRD-SEI-214 — Connections, registration and routing, FR1–27
Primary connection, readiness, route, concurrency and historical-context requirements. Initial scope is legal entity, direction, environment and effective time; advanced routing is not approved.
PRD-SEI-213 — Private connectivity and PRD-SEI-235 — Provider API
Customer-provider integration and qualified Provider API, Sage adapter or hybrid modes. A mode name does not establish provider readiness.
PRD-SEI-210 — Sage as a private platform, capability/reuse boundaries
Proposed operator expansion using the earlier foundation. Investment, accountable operator and build/partner route remain open.
PRD-SEI-223 — Exchange, FR1–5/12–26
Recipient evidence, immutable exchange plans, independent actions, interconnection and safe recovery. Exchange owns the invoice/action plan, rather than this foundation creating another one.
PRD-SEI-221 — Operator readiness, PRD-SEI-215 — Recovery
Operator eligibility and recovery evidence gates; no new legal clock or external API is defined here.
PRD-SEI-227 — Shared platform and FP-SEI-001 — Reuse assessment
Shared design direction and implementation qualification. Written requirements do not prove a production implementation.

ac:layout-cell.p: In scope: role-qualified connection profiles, separate registration observations and capability checks, controlled activation, deterministic route selection, adapter handoffs, suspension, migration qualification and historical dependencies. Open/gated expansion: operator interconnection, direct private exchange and a public bridge use the same model only after applicable evidence and approval. Connecting to providers first is a delivery sequence, not a technical prerequisite to operating a platform.

Out of scope: legal invoice issuance, a new Global API product, a new invoice store, provider endpoint design, approval of operator launch, general routing optimisation, per-invoice caller override, automatic failover, approval of Private A → Private B customer switching, signing/transformation implementation and final retention/deletion. Platform-to-platform invoice exchange is different from changing a customer's selected platform.

The supplied public WSDLs can qualify the SPFE adapter portion of a connection profile. They do not qualify private-provider interfaces, operator accreditation, customer enrolment or receiving-point publication. This review changes only the public binding of the shared model.

See REF Source references for the original files, exact locations and source limits. The technical evidence guide tracks shared source conflicts. The constraints below align this feature with the supplied public evidence; Sage implementation and activation remain gated.

tr.td: Connection / registration / readiness / route
Communication configuration; observed external enrolment or reachability; evidence for a selected capability; time-bound platform selection for a defined invoice scope. These are separate facts.
Integration role
The capacity in which Sage uses an interface: customer-provider integration or platform interconnection. The role selects qualified contracts and controls; it does not grant customer authority.
Contract profile
Selected operation, protocol/schema, environment, destination and safety rules. It is separate from invoice format and operator eligibility.
Exchange action
One separately tracked delivery, public-copy submission or event report, with its own result.
Cutover / historical continuity
The boundary when future eligible work changes platform; the permitted actors, access and evidence retained for earlier invoices.
Authenticated principal / represented party
Trusted caller identity; business or person on whose behalf the action is performed. They are checked separately.
Shared connection records, profiles, checks and route versions
Proposed Connection / Routing logical owners within Domain Services. Actual service/build ownership stays open under SPC-Q01.
Customer setup and platform-change journey
SPEC-SEI-002 owns customer intent and journey results; uses this foundation for readiness and route commit. SPEC-SEI-003 owns exit and dependency release.
Common API access
SPEC-SEI-013 exposes authorised operations and results; it does not implement a second route engine.
Public protocol access
SPEC-SEI-011 owns public operation execution and evidence. This foundation supplies qualified connection/route context, not a replacement public connector.
Invoice exchange and recipient resolution
SPEC-SEI-007 owns the final exchange plan/actions; SPEC-SEI-012 supplies recipient evidence; SPEC-SEI-016 owns trusted intake and product delivery.
Status facts and required reports
SPEC-SEI-009 interprets events and owns reporting obligations. Resolve permitted historical context here without changing the fact or replaying a report.
Trust and transformation
SPEC-SEI-001 owns protected credentials/trust. Existing DTS is the preferred transformation reuse candidate; SPEC-SEI-008 does not qualify every input/output pair.

ac:layout-cell.p: For every candidate record its source implementation or design pattern, retained behaviour, local changes, missing coverage, owner and evidence. Reusing an implementation requires actual build/contract results; copying a proposed pattern does not establish production readiness.
Diagram step names use plain-language actions. The smaller activity references link to the detailed behaviour and checks below.

Text equivalent: authorised customer/administrator request → SPC-01 establish business and role → SPC-02 save connection/profile independently from the active route → SPC-03 check each capability and observed external state → return setup result with passed checks, limitations and required actions. Missing evidence blocks only the affected capability; an uncertain external change goes to SPC-07 before repetition. Even a fully qualified connection cannot change the customer's platform without SPC-04.

Text equivalent: explicit platform-change request → SPC-04 prepare and commit the authorised direction/effective boundary after current qualification and external confirmation → SPC-05 resolve a single route for new work → SPC-06 bind the route/profile to the owning invoice/action before external processing. A conflict or uncertain external change goes to SPC-07. SPC-08 preserves permitted historical work and applies suspension/release checks. A qualified future route does not replace earlier invoice context.

ac:layout-cell.p: SPC-Q01–Q07 gate actual component reuse, external contracts, country/operator controls, incoming reachability, continuity, operating limits and delivery scope. This spec changes no live route. A customer sees setup result and required actions or platform-change result; an internal readiness label never promises that a route is already active.

The proposed logical records use existing concepts: connection, registration observation, capability qualification, route/version, transition, immutable invoice context and continuity dependency. Add integration role and contract-profile references rather than parallel Phase 2/Phase 3 record families. Logical field names here are proposed; actual mappings need SPC-Q01. Preserve existing contracts until compatibility is proven.

Connection configuration, qualification, selected route and operator eligibility remain independently visible. Keep UNKNOWN for unproven registration and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN for a possible external effect with no reliable result. A failed probe is not evidence that registration ended. Do not introduce a customer-wide readiness flag or a universal external state mapping.

ol.li: Every access and mutation checks tenant, represented party, authenticated caller, environment, capability and current authority. Operator approval cannot replace customer authority.
Readiness is qualified for the exact role, contract/profile and capability. Customer-interface success cannot activate platform interconnection.
Preparing or qualifying a connection never changes a route. Route activation and external registration are separate operations with separate evidence.
A scoped route has one eligible connection for each decision time. Reject overlapping effective periods or ambiguous matches; do not use database order or invent fallback.

Before external processing, the owning feature saves the effective route/profile and the action's execution owner. A route change cannot rewrite that record or move an uncertain action to a second executor.
Earlier work uses recorded context and separately verified current historical authority. Old credentials or provider access are not retained indefinitely merely because records exist.
Required public copies and event reports have independent actions/results under country policy. Connection readiness does not create these obligations.

ac:layout-cell.p: SPC-01 — Establish scope and role. On a product/partner request, verify the authenticated principal's capability and represented-party grant. Resolve tenant/legal entity, country, trusted environment and requested direction. Reject caller-supplied conflicting identity/environment or unauthorised role selection before exposing records. Operator administration may qualify a platform profile without access to customer invoice data; customer route activation still needs the customer's authority and entitlement. Save decision source/version and rejection reason with sensitive values removed.

SPC-02 — Configure the connection. Validate the chosen provider/network and supported integration mode (PROVIDER_API, SAGE_ADAPTER or qualified HYBRID). Save configuration under expected version and request identity; protect credential references through SPEC-SEI-001. The profile identifies role, operation, protocol/schema version, approved destination reference, trust/authority requirements, accepted representation/profile, limits, idempotency/query support and execution/reconciliation owners. Do not accept arbitrary caller URLs. Same request identity/content returns the prior result; changed content conflicts. Multiple roles may share proven adapter code, but require distinct bindings where authority, accounts or interfaces differ. Updating a credential/profile invalidates affected qualification until checked; it cannot mutate existing invoice context.

SPC-03 — Qualify each capability. Adapter/Connection owners assess incoming, outgoing, status, notification and reconciliation paths independently. Use approved checks that do not issue invoices or mutate registration. Store check result, source, observed time, rule/profile/credential version, expiry/recheck condition and limitations. Where enrolment or receiving-point publication requires a mutation, its feature owns a durable operation and independent observation; configured, acknowledged and observed reachable remain separate results. Ambiguous publication enters SPC-07. Missing provider observation requires an approved manual evidence gate, not inferred success. No global READY promotion is allowed from one successful call. Return passed/failed/unknown checks and named required actions; expose no credentials.

For platform interconnection, also qualify operator eligibility, peer identity, selected trust/transport, supported invoice/status operations, test evidence and responsible support owner. An interconnection case being opened or closed is not technical readiness. No legal deadline or protocol is asserted by this spec; the applicable rule and external artefacts remain SPC-Q02/Q03 gates.

SPC-04 — Change e-invoicing platform. On an explicit authorised customer/delegate request, identify sending, receiving or both; display current and proposed platform, effective boundary, limitations and historical impact. Onboarding/exit owns this customer journey; Routing owns the single route commit. Recheck current authority, entitlement, role qualification, dependency validity and expected route version. Prevent overlapping active/scheduled scopes and serialise competing changes through the existing Routing owner.

Prepare any required external receiving-point change with durable request identity and observed result before declaring activation. There is no distributed atomicity assumption: save preparation state, reconcile a possible external effect, and hold affected work where external and local selections disagree. Commit the local route with an expected-version check only when the contract-specific ordering and reachability checks pass. Return result per direction, actual boundary and remaining historical tasks. Unaffected directions continue. Cancellation before external effect leaves the old route; after a possible effect it requires reconciliation. Restoration after cutover is a new authorised transition, not deletion of evidence or a rewrite of the previous boundary. Private A → Private B customer switching remains disabled until the source product decision and its transition contract are approved.

SPC-05 — Resolve new work. For new work, apply the route's effective interval to the trusted decision time and implemented scope: legal entity, direction and environment within tenant/country. Exclude ineligible capabilities using current role/profile evidence. Return exactly one route/version with selection reason. No match returns an owned hold under the approved no-route policy; several matches return a configuration conflict. A timeout is not proof of no private destination. Outbound Exchange separately resolves recipient evidence and applies Spain delivery/copy policy through SPEC-SEI-012/007. A customer-provider route and the recipient's destination are different selections; do not merge them. For incoming traffic, Receiving matches the authenticated source and permitted receiving interval, rather than treating the current outbound route as authorisation.

SPC-06 — Bind and hand off. Return connection/profile version, permitted executor, protected references and decision evidence to the owning feature. Exchange/Receiving stores immutable invoice context before external processing. Exchange plans independent delivery/copy/reporting actions where applicable, each with one execution and reconciliation owner. A partner work claim under SPEC-SEI-013 and an adapter under SPEC-SEI-011 must not execute the same action concurrently. The selected executor validates current authority and credential safety immediately before transmission, while preserving the original action identity/profile; a changed contract requires explicit recovery, not silent replacement. Receiving validates the actual source/file under SPEC-SEI-016. Record external references and exact acknowledgement meaning through the owning feature. Transport success is not buyer acceptance, payment or report completion.

SPC-07 — Reconcile and recover. The operation owner records whether an external change may have happened. For a lost response, claim expiry, conflicting observation or stale commit, use the original operation/profile/reference to query authoritative state where supported. Repeat a mutation only under a proven repeat contract; otherwise retain an owned unresolved case with escalation. Do not switch to a new platform or credential merely because a worker lease expired. Safe read rechecks may refresh qualification under approved limits. Manual action needs scoped permission, evidence, reason and audit; it cannot invent external completion. After correction, requalify only the affected capability and separately request route activation if needed. Feature-specific recovery remains in SPEC-SEI-002/007/009/011/013/016; this foundation owns connection/route discrepancy recovery without duplicating their action stores.

SPC-08 — Preserve continuity and suspend/release. Before disablement, list active/scheduled routes and in-flight/historical dependencies. Revoked authority or unsafe trust stops protected actions; keeping a record does not retain permission. Route historical work using the original invoice/operator context and an approved current actor/channel. Missing historical authority opens a continuity case rather than silently using the new platform. A contract-approved replacement channel is an append-only handoff with evidence and owner, not a rewrite of the original invoice snapshot. SPEC-SEI-003 coordinates deregistration, credential release, export, retention and deletion at their own gates. Rollout of the operator role must preserve existing customer-provider connections; qualifying the new role does not activate it or migrate customers.

ac:layout-cell.p: Encrypt protected records and transport under approved policy; return credential handles, never secrets. Restrict endpoints and parser/file access in the owning adapter/receiving service. Audit actor, reason, before/after version, correlation and evidence reference without raw invoice content. Operations views require separate permission. Measure qualification freshness, transition age, conflicting/unknown operations, historical dependencies, backlog and provider health without business identifiers in metric labels. SPC-Q06 gates quotas, expiry/recheck, retention, retry budgets and service targets; no numeric commitment is invented.

The source facts below govern the public binding. Recovery, storage and qualification actions are proposed Sage controls where stated. Apply them through SPC-02–03, SPC-06–07. Source conflicts stay open under SPC-Q02/Q03/Q04; SPFE-Q09/Q12; they are not resolved by a local default.

tr.td: SPC-SPFE-R01 Qualify only the evidenced public profile

SPC-02/03 records the exact SPFE operation, WSDL version/port, certificate class, represented-party authority and environment. Public readiness cannot qualify a private provider or operator role, publish an entry point or activate a customer route. PRE addresses remain separate from production evidence.
SPFE-S03/SPFE-S16; REF.
SPC-SPFE-R02 Preserve owning-feature public action rules

SPC-06 passes the frozen action to one public executor. OUT owns the Article 3/4 copy decision and LCS owns reporting. Public interconnection must not create a redundant faithful copy. Invoice-query absence cannot become recipient-routing evidence or permission to switch routes.
SPFE-S02/SPFE-S03; proposed execution boundary; REF.

ac:layout-cell.h2: Part 3 Logical Service Interactions and Data Inventory
ac:layout-cell.p: All mutations carry scoped caller/represented-party context, request identity, input digest and expected version. Save a stable local operation receipt before possible external change. Read results state observation time and uncertainty. These are logical contracts, not approved endpoints.

ac:layout-cell.p: The scenarios below are checks to run, not claims that they passed on a deployed implementation. Activity numbers refer to SPC-01–08; interaction/data numbers refer to the inventories above.

tr.td: SPC-A01 Add operator role without replacing the foundation

An existing customer-provider connection keeps identity, selected routes and history when a separately qualified operator profile is added. Shared owner/model/contracts are evidenced; no duplicate route engine or invoice store.
SPC-A02 No qualification inheritance between roles
Customer-interface success leaves operator interconnection unqualified until its own trust, contract and operator checks pass; incompatible credentials cannot cross roles.
SPC-A03 Configure/check without platform change
Setup returns passed, failed and unknown checks with required action/owner; public/private routes remain unchanged. No test issues an invoice.
SPC-A04 Scope and isolation denial
Cross-tenant/entity/country/environment, forged role and revoked grant requests fail before protected access/send; no credential or object-existence leakage.
SPC-A05 Independent direction and concurrency
Private sending/public receiving coexist. Competing or overlapping changes cannot both commit; unaffected directions continue and results state the actual scope.
SPC-A06 Ambiguous publication, cancellation and restoration

Lost external response holds affected activation and observes the original operation before repeat. Pre-effect cancellation keeps the old route; post-effect cancellation reconciles; restoration appends a new authorised boundary.
SPC-A07 Deterministic selection and separate recipient lookup
Zero/multiple matches return owned hold/conflict. Recipient lookup failure does not invent public fallback or override the customer's provider. Route/profile context persists before processing.
SPC-A08 Single executor and unknown-action recovery
Partner claim and adapter cannot send one action twice; expiry or timeout does not move it to a second executor. Public-copy/report failure does not resend successful invoice delivery.
SPC-A09 Historical continuity and suspension

After a platform change, earlier delivery/status/reporting uses original context plus current permission. Revocation blocks unsafe access; an unresolved actor/channel prevents dependent release and stays visible.
SPC-A10 Country isolation and implementation qualification

A separate country binding does not inherit Spain identity, recipient, copy or reporting rules. Existing build/contracts/mappings/operations and gaps are recorded; unsupported role/profile/DTS pair stays disabled.
SPC-A11 Operator exchange is distinct from customer switching
Qualifying a peer interconnection does not migrate customers, enable Private A → Private B switching or activate the Sage proposition. Evidence gates remain explicit.
SPC-A12 Durable results and permitted operations view

A crash after save permits result/notification recovery without repeating a mutation. Scoped support sees intended/observed state, evidence age and safe owner/action; secrets and other customers' data remain hidden.
SPC-Q01 Actual Connection/Routing/API build, record mappings, service owners and migration fit
Architecture + Connection/Routing/API owners: contracts/builds, baseline, gaps and compatibility proof.
Blocks build-ready physical design and implementation-reuse claims; select existing owners before adding components.
SPC-Q02 External interface per provider, role and capability
Integration/provider/public-connector owners: exact operation, initiator, profile, credentials, conformance and query/repeat semantics.
Blocks affected adapter/profile activation; common provider identity does not prove common interface.
SPC-Q03 Spain country rules and operator eligibility
Spain Product/Compliance + accountable operator: approved identity/routing/copy/reporting rules, interconnection applicability and operator evidence.
Blocks country-dependent/operator activation; no new legal interpretation is established here.
SPC-Q04 Incoming reachability and external/local cutover ordering
Routing/Onboarding + provider owners: publication observations, expiry, mismatch recovery, cancellation and restoration tests.
Blocks affected receiving cutover; outbound qualification cannot substitute for it.
SPC-Q05 Historical actor/channel and dependency release
Lifecycle/exit/Records + Compliance/providers: current authority, approved replacement channel, continuity and release evidence.
Blocks unsafe historical execution or release; preserve an owned unresolved case.
SPC-Q06 Operational and data-policy targets
Operations/Security/Records + Product: measured volume, provider limits, freshness/retry policy, monitoring, retention and support/runbooks.
Blocks production sign-off and numeric commitments.
SPC-Q07 First delivery cohort and expansion scope
Spain Product + Architecture/operator owners: provider/role/direction matrix, approved product scope and controlled rollout.
Pilot only qualified capabilities; per-invoice override, automatic failover and Private A → Private B customer switching remain outside initial scope.

ac:layout-cell.p: Reviewable logical proposal. Design review can assess one foundation and its separate role/country bindings. Pilot requires SPC-Q01/Q02/Q04 plus applicable SPC-Q03 decisions, isolation/concurrency/unknown-outcome acceptance and continuity owners. Production and operator expansion additionally require actual operator approval, implementation qualification, measured operating controls and supported historical/exit paths. No publication, status change, operator investment or live activation is implied.

These are required evidence scenarios, not executed implementation tests. The source-binding gate is SPC-Q02/Q03/Q04; SPFE-Q09/Q12. A source-backed review does not establish that this feature is ready for production.

ac:layout-cell.p: For public-platform legal and external-contract facts, the original official sources below take precedence over earlier assumptions in linked PRDs and internal notes. PRDs retain product scope and are unchanged by this review. A source conflict remains an explicit gate; this spec cannot approve a local substitute.

Use the original files for the claims they establish. Final published regulation governs legal requirements; technical files supply their stated contract facts. Examples are illustrative. Missing or conflicting evidence remains a named gate. Product requirements and Sage design controls have separate authority. The English guide and extracts are reading aids.
